State of New Mexico

Michelle Lujan Grisham
Governor

EXECUTIVE ORDER 2026-078
AUTHORIZING ADDITIONAL EMERGENCY FUNDS FOR THE NEW MEXICO
NATIONAL GUARD DUE TO EMERGENCY IN RIO ARRIBA COUNTY, SANTA FE
COUNTY, TAOS COUNTY, THE CITY OF ESPANOLA, THE JICARILLA APACHE
RESERVATION, AND THE PUEBLOS OF POJOAQUE, OHKAY OWINGEH, SANTA
CLARA, SAN ILDEFONSO AND TESUQUE

WHEREAS, Rio Arriba County, Santa Fe County, Taos County, the City of Espafiola and
neighboring pueblos, and the Jicarilla Apache Reservation are experiencing a significant increase
in crime, including but not limited to violent offenses, property crimes, drug trafficking, and other
public safety threats;

WHEREAS, for example, police calls in the City of Espafiola—which straddles Santa Fe
and Rio Arriba Counties—have more than doubled in the past two years, and police dispatches to
businesses in Santa Clara have quadrupled during that same time;

WHEREAS, the impacts of these public safety threats are severe and far-reaching,
manifesting in increased homelessness, family instability, and fatal drug overdoses;

WHEREAS, a significant number of residents of Rio Arriba County, Espafiola, Santa
Clara, and Ohkay Owingeh struggle with addiction to alcohol and illicit substances such as
fentanyl, resulting in Rio Arriba County having the highest overdose death rate in the state;

WHEREAS, the surge in criminal activity and addiction has placed an extraordinary

burden on the local governments, especially local police departments;

State Capitol + Room 400 + Santa Fe, New Mexico 87501 * 505-476-2200

 WHEREAS, | have recently issued executive orders declaring a state of emergency in Rio
Arriba County, Santa Fe County, Taos County, the City of Espafiola, the Jicarilla Apache
Reservation, and the Pueblos of Pojoaque, Ohkay Owingeh, Santa Clara, San Ildefonso, and
Tesuque after they indicated that local resources are insufficient to address this emergency and
requested assistance from the State of New Mexico;

WHEREAS, these previous orders released emergency funds to the Department of
Homeland Security and Emergency Management and directed the Adjutant General to order into
service any elements of the New Mexico National Guard as are or may be needed to provide
military support to civil authorities as needed for this emergency;

WHEREAS, the New Mexico National Guard possesses the personnel, logistical
capabilities, and resources necessary to provide non-law enforcement support this effort, including
assistance with traffic control, administrative duties, prisoner transport, court security, emergency
response, and other critical functions that allow local law enforcement to focus on crime reduction
efforts;

WHEREAS, the New Mexico National Guard requires additional funding to provide this
critical support;

WHEREAS, this emergency requires immediate action to protect public peace, health, and
safety; and

WHEREAS, this disaster is of such magnitude as to be beyond local control and requires
the resources of the State of New Mexico to minimize economic or physical harm and to take
actions necessary to protect the public health, safety, and welfare.

NOW, THEREFORE, I, Michelle Lujan Grisham, Governor of the State of New Mexico,

by virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the laws of the State of New Mexico

Executive Order 2026-078 Page 2

State Capitol * Room400 + Santa Fe, New Mexico 87501 + 505-476-2200

 do hereby DECLARE a state of emergency to exist in Rio Arriba County, Santa Fe County, Taos
County, the City of Espafiola, the Jicarilla Apache Reservation, and the Pueblos of Pojoaque,
Obkay Owingeh, Santa Clara, San Ildefonso, and Tesuque, and ORDER and DIRECT as follows:

1. The Department of Finance and Administration shall make available additional
emergency financial resources in an amount not to exceed three hundred and fifty thousand dollars
($350,000.00) to the New Mexico National Guard in accordance with NMSA 1978, Sections 12-
11-23 to -25, and NMSA 1978, Sections 12-10-14 to -15. Such funds shall be expended for the
purposes of. avoiding or minimizing economic and physical harm; protecting the public health,
safety, welfare; and providing emergency and disaster relief, including but not limited to the
payment of any expense incident to the provision of humanitarian relief and other assistance to
civil authorities. Such funds shall be paid out upon warrants drawn by the Secretary of Finance
and Administration upon vouchers approved by the Governor, or an agent or agency designated
by her for that purpose.

2. The Adjutant General shall order into service any elements of the New Mexico
National Guard as are or may be needed to provide military support to civil authorities as needed
for this emergency. This action is pursuant to and in accordance with NMSA 1978, Sections 20-
1-1 to -8, NMSA 1978, Sections 20-2-1 to -8, NMSA 1978, Section 20-3-2(E), and NMSA 1978,
Sections 20-4-1 to -14. Such emergency assistance shall be provided during the period of need at
the discretion of the Governor or her Authorized Representative.

I FURTHER ORDER and DIRECT as follows:

1. This Order supersedes any previous orders, proclamations, or directives to the

extent they are in conflict.

Executive Order 2026-078 Page 3

State Capitol * Room400 + Santa Fe, New Mexico 87501 + 505-476-2200

 2. This Order shall take effect immediately and shall remain in effect until all

authorized funds are expended or no longer necessary to provide emergency assistance.

ATTEST: DONE AT THE EXECUTIVE OFFICE

. 4 ’ CL, THIS 8TH DAY OF OCTOBER 2026
MAGGIE TOULOUSE OLIVER WITNESS MY HAND AND THE GREAT
SECRETARY OF STATE SEAL OF THE STATE OF NEW MEXICO
